item.text: {"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"For 2023, movement toward the ruler’s stated development, welfare, and security goals was mixed and weakly attributable. The government-linked PDL-145T reported 300–400 works ready by August, but this was an official progress claim without independent verification of completion, service quality, distribution, or budget execution; a separate evaluation found only 50% of the multi-year Joint Resilience Programme’s planned activities fully implemented and attributed improvements mainly to that programme rather than to Tshisekedi personally (BATCH-0019-E009; BATCH-0002-E002). Education enrollment had increased under the free-primary-education policy, but the trend began in 2019 and does not establish 2023-specific or presidential effects; broader tenure evidence also reports persistent low preschool attendance and more than 7.5 million children out of school (BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0028-E020). Economic output was reported at 6.2%, and 2023 revenue and expenditure execution were substantial, but aggregate fiscal execution does not show that spending advanced the frozen goals or was effectively controlled. Inflation reached 33.9% at year end, the franc depreciated by more than 28% during 2023, and the president acknowledged that purchasing-power gains had not been sufficiently felt (BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0015-E004). Distributional and welfare outcomes remained adverse: more than 25 million people faced acute food insecurity, displacement exceeded 5.6 million in the eastern provinces and reached 6.8–6.9 million nationally, while conflict and limited rural investment disrupted agriculture and infrastructure (BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0013-E014; BATCH-0010-E003). Security outcomes moved substantially away from the stated territorial-integrity and stability goals: M23 gained territory, violence involving M23 rose 29% from 2022 after a ceasefire breakdown, and late-2023 fighting produced mass displacement. These outcomes remain attribution-sensitive because armed groups, Rwanda and other regional actors, international-force changes, inherited fragility, global economic shocks, donors, and humanitarian agencies materially shaped results (BATCH-0027-E006; BATCH-0006-E002; BATCH-0013-E014; BATCH-0002-E002; BATCH-0025-E003). Overall, the evidence supports limited, mixed progress in selected outputs but not clear ruler-attributed improvement in outcomes or distribution across the broader portfolio during the 2023 period.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E009","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0022-E004","BATCH-0010-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0027-E006","BATCH-0006-E002","BATCH-0025-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most indicators are national, multi-year, or reported for the ruler’s broader tenure rather than isolating within-2023 change from a defined baseline.","Official PDL-145T and presidential claims are not independently verified here; fiscal execution measures spending volume, not goal alignment, distribution, quality, or presidential control.","Security, welfare, education, and health outcomes are confounded by armed groups, regional intervention, international and humanitarian actors, donor resources, global shocks, and inherited conditions.","The supplied evidence does not establish a complete counterfactual or realistic lag-adjusted causal estimate for Tshisekedi’s policies."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported inference that reported PDL-145T works were completed and that aggregate fiscal execution itself represented progress toward the ruler’s goals.","Recast education and welfare gains as policy- or programme-associated, often pre-2023 and not president-specific.","Separated 2023 year-end and late-2023 outcomes from multi-year or tenure-wide indicators.","Added the supplied evidence on purchasing-power decline, food insecurity, poverty, displacement, and weak translation of growth into living conditions.","Retained security deterioration while explicitly limiting personal attribution and identifying external and inherited causes."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review is warranted if independently verified PDL-145T completion, service-use, distributional, or audit evidence becomes available.","A baseline-and-counterfactual analysis could clarify which 2023 changes were attributable to presidential decisions rather than pre-existing trends, donor programmes, or conflict and macroeconomic shocks.","Further evidence is needed on within-period implementation, policy correction, and outcomes across material program components."]}
